transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I don’t really care about anything anymore. Things I used to like—my art classes, board-game nights, hiking, even trying to get back on the soccer team—I just don’t feel anything for them now. I mostly sit in my room and watch everything kind of slip away.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or euphoric?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt a little better than usual, but not unusually energetic or euphoric like that.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for a couple of weeks or longer?

I’m not sure about another time before this. What I know is right now I just don’t care about anything anymore—art classes, board-game nights, hiking, even trying to get back into soccer. I mostly just sit in my room and let everything slide.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?
Yes. Most days I wake up feeling really heavy inside… like this hollow feeling in my chest. It feels like there isn’t much of a future for me outside these apartment walls.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of killing yourself?
Yes… I keep having thoughts that I just don’t want to wake up anymore. And when my friend found me, I was saying out loud that I couldn’t keep living like this.
Before this current episode, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I don’t really know. I can’t remember another clear time like this before. Right now is the main thing I can point to.
Because of how you’ve been feeling, have you been unable to manage your usual daily responsibilities?

Yes. I’ve pretty much stopped taking freelance art-education jobs. I’m missing community events and soccer, things I normally would show up for. And honestly, my friend has been checking on me because I’m not reliably eating or showering, and I don’t feel like I can always keep myself safe.
Did this start soon after a major stressful event or big life change?
Yes. It started pretty soon after my divorce. It’s been going on since then… about a year and eleven months now.
Since this began after your divorce, has there been any period of at least two months when you felt mostly back to your usual self?

No, not really. Since shortly after the divorce it’s just kind of stayed with me. It’s been about a year and eleven months now, and I don’t think there’s been a two-month stretch where I felt like my usual self.
Before your divorce, was there ever a time when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I had rough times before, but I can’t clearly say there was a two-week period like that before the divorce.
For the past two years, have you felt depressed most days?
Yes. Most days I wake up feeling really low… like there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It feels like there isn’t much of a future for me beyond my apartment.
Do your feelings since the divorce seem much stronger than you would expect for what happened?
Yes… I think it does feel stronger. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, and it’s like I can’t see any real future for myself beyond my apartment walls.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?

Yes. Some days I can’t sit still and I pace from the kitchen to the window over and over until my legs hurt. Other times I’m the opposite… I move so slowly that even making coffee feels like I’m lifting wet cement.
When you feel at your lowest, have you heard voices or become convinced of things that other people say aren’t true?

Yes. A lot of this past year, when I’ve been really low, the voices are there too. I’ll be lying in bed feeling hopeless, and I hear this woman saying I ruined everything. It feels very real when it’s happening.
Have you ever heard that woman’s voice at a time when you were not feeling depressed?

Yes. There was a stretch before the depression got really bad where I wasn’t feeling as low yet. I could still cook sometimes, and I’d answer friends. But I was already hearing that woman’s voice, and for weeks I was also thinking the hallway lights were signals about me.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the woman’s voice or believing the hallway lights were sending signals about you, while you were not feeling depressed?

Yes. It was before the really bad depression hit. For a few weeks, I wasn’t feeling that low yet—I could still cook sometimes and answer friends—but I was already hearing her voice, and I thought the hallway lights were sending signals about me.
Even when you were not feeling depressed, did you still have a strong loss of motivation or interest in things?

Yes. Even when I wasn’t feeling deeply depressed, I still just… didn’t care about anything. I stopped caring about my art classes, board-game nights, hiking, even trying to get back on the soccer team. I mostly just sit in my room and let things slip away.
For most of the time since this started, have the voices or the feeling that the hallway lights were sending signals been present even when you were not depressed?

Yes, there was that stretch before the depression got really bad. I could still do some normal things, like cook sometimes and answer friends, but I was already hearing her voice and thinking the hallway lights were sending signals about me. That went on for weeks.
Did there ever come a time when the voices or the sense that the hallway lights were sending signals lasted for a full month while you were not feeling depressed?

Yes… I think so. There was that time before the depression got really bad where I could still do some normal things, like cook once in a while and answer friends. But the voice was already there, and I was already thinking the hallway lights were sending signals about me. That went on for weeks.
Was there ever a full month when you were hearing the voice or thought the hallway lights were sending signals, and you were not depressed at all during that time?

Yes. Before the depression got really bad, there was a stretch where I wasn’t feeling depressed like that. I could still cook sometimes and answer friends. But I was already hearing the voice, and I really thought the hallway lights were sending signals about me. That went on for weeks… about a month, I think.
